report.source_text: The patient underwent additional pelvic and transvaginal ultrasound, an abdominal and pelvic CT, and a pelvic MRI with and without intravenous contrast. The MRI findings revealed a solid mass measuring 10.5 × 9.5 × 11.3 cm anterior to the uterine fundus with numerous internal non-enhancing cystic spaces. The mass slightly abuts the anterior uterine fundus but appears to cause mass effect on the uterus. Immediately inferior to this 11 cm mass, a tubular cystic lesion measuring 3.2 × 5.2 × 5.3 cm was found. The uterus was also found to be anteverted, slightly anteflexed, and normal-sized. The findings also included a right ovarian cyst measuring 1.1 cm. The 11 cm solid mass was presumed to represent a pedunculated partially necrotic fibroid that had torsed and disconnected from the uterus. Radiology recommended surgical resection.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old postmenopausal woman presented to the emergency department with intense pelvic and abdominal pain radiating to the lower back, vomiting, diarrhea, and urinary symptoms (E001, E002). Initial transabdominal pelvic ultrasound revealed uterine fibroids measuring 10.1 × 9.7 × 11.5 cm, and because a previous ultrasound 15 days prior had visualized both ovaries, the risk of ovarian torsion was deemed low; she was discharged with gynecology follow-up (E002). A few days later, she returned to her OB-GYN with severe pain in the lower abdomen, right groin, and right buttock with occasional nausea (E003). Preoperative imaging including pelvic MRI revealed a 10.5 × 9.5 × 11.3 cm solid mass anterior to the uterine fundus with cystic spaces, presumed to represent a pedunculated partially necrotic fibroid that had torsed (E004). Surgical exploration revealed a partially torsioned right adnexal mass measuring 14 × 10 × 10 cm with cystic degeneration and hemorrhage; the right ovary was not observed separate from the mass. Intraoperative diagnosis confirmed a right ovarian fibroma, contrasting with the preoperative imaging interpretation of uterine leiomyoma (E005). Postoperative course was uneventful, and cytology and pathology reports were negative for malignancy (E006).
